chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you wish to embalm the deceased, apply camphor to him, wiping with it the marks of prostration on his body, all his joints, his head, his beard, and upon his chest with the embalming mixture.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The embalming of the man and the woman is the same.
And he (peace be upon him) said: And I dislike that it be followed by the (smoke of) incense burning.

key_terms.آثَارَ السُّجُودِ: Marks of prostration (areas of the body touching the ground during prayer)
key_terms.تُحَنِّطَ: To embalm or apply camphor to the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the proper method for applying camphor to the deceased according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual significance of preserving the physical marks of worship, specifically directing the application of camphor to the sites of prostration (sujood) to honor the deceased's devotion. It further clarifies that this ritual is gender-neutral and expresses a preference against using incense burners (mijmarah), reflecting early Shia juristic discussions on the simplicity and purity of burial rites. The instruction highlights the continuity of the body's sanctity from life to death, linking physical preparation to spiritual reverence.
